messages:
maria: Quick thread — proposal: make telemetry scrub rules routing-aware and tier-aware. Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private should get different attribute sets + retention. Thoughts?
aj: +1 on tiers. Concern: adding routing metadata to spans will spike cardinality if we add route names verbatim.
leo: Can we add a low-cardinality shim like `route_bucket` (e.g. hash(route) -> 32 buckets) instead of full route names? keeps debugability but limits cardinality.
kira: We also need to consider provenance: if Dedicated customers expect more raw attrs for debugging, we should allow an opt-in retention window inside their VPC. For hosted, default to hashed IDs + aggressive TTL.
maria: Exactly. Proposal sketch: 1) At collector ingest, map detailed route -> small bucket id. 2) Keep salted prompt-hash and request_id-hash, but store a `retention_bucket` per request = deterministic function(route_bucket, customer_tier, random-sample). 3) Retention policy table decides TTL and exporter targets.
aj: Who does the hashing/salting? collector vs aggregator? If collector does it we lose flexibility later. If aggregator does it we keep raw longer (PII risk).
leo: Tradeoff: do minimal scrubbing at edge (drop raw prompt text), but keep request_id raw behind KMS until aggregator applies HMAC for bucketing. Means edge never emits plaintext prompts.
kira: We need key rotation rules for HMAC used in hashing request_ids/prompt hashes. Suggested: rotate keys monthly and keep old keys for decryption of metadata only for 90 days. Also record key-id on spans.
telemetry-bot: config suggestion: `sampler.route_bucket = fn(route) => murmur3(route) % 32` and `attr_scrub.rules: - match: prompt_text action: redact keep_hash: true`
sam: UX ask: Console should surface per-route sample rate + retained fields. For canary rollouts, engineers need to temporarily elevate retention for a route for 1h and then auto-revert.
maria: +1 console elevation. Also add an audit log entry and require two-person approval for >24h retention changes on hosted.
aj: For billing/quotas: we must ensure retention upgrades don't bypass quota accounting. Maybe record an immutable metric token like `telemetry_units` per trace that counts cost so billing aligns.
leo: Implementation detail: exporter pipeline — keep two streams: low-cardinality telemetry (long retention, aggregated) and escalated raw-traces (short TTL, restricted access). Use routing policy to copy traces to raw-trace stream only if retention_bucket permits.
kira: Sampling key composition idea: `sampling_key = HMAC(key, request_id || route_bucket || tier)` so samples for a given request deterministically fall into same bucket across retries.
maria: Yep. Also add a small sampler that favors errors and new model variants (model_version tag) — higher retention for those.
aj: Ops question: will our current OTel collector processors support route_bucket insertion cheaply? we can add a processor plugin that maps route->bucket using a small lookup and murmur3 fallback.
leo: I'll prototype a collector processor. Pseudoconfig in thread: ```yaml
processors:
  route_bucket:
    type: route_bucket
    buckets: 32
    field: http.route
```
kira: Tests: we need unit tests ensuring bucket distribution and end-to-end integration test that asserted no raw prompt text ends up in hosted long-term store.
maria: Agree. Next steps: 1) leo prototype collector processor PR, 2) aj draft key rotation & KMS flow, 3) kira draft retention policy matrix (tier x bucket -> TTL/exporter). I'll open RFC doc.
sam: UX follow-up: I'll mock console elevation flow + audit modal.
maria: Great — schedule 30m sync after PRs land. Thanks all :thumbsup:
telemetry-bot: NOTE: created RFC draft at /docs/rfc/1793451230-route-aware-telemetry.md (private)
